extractedItems.title: What happens if you accidentally move your ball on the green?
extractedItems.question: On the green, if you accidentally move your ball while taking a practice swing too close to it, what should you do?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position, no penalty
Put the ball back with no penalty
Put the ball back and add a penalty stroke
Leave the ball and skip your turn

extractedItems.explanation: If you accidentally move your ball on the green, there is no penalty but you must put it back to its original spot.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer accidentally nudging her ball on the green with her putter and then carefully replacing it.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Girl golfer replaces moved golf ball on the green.

extractedItems.title: Penalty for playing the wrong ball
extractedItems.question: You realise that you have played a shot with a ball that isn’t yours while out on the course. What do you need to do next?

choices.text: Keep playing with the wrong ball
Go back and play your correct ball, ignoring strokes with the wrong ball, but take 2 penalty strokes
Go back to the last tee and start again
Replace the wrong ball where you found it

extractedItems.explanation: You must play your correct ball and are given two penalty strokes, but the strokes with the wrong ball do not count.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer realising he played a ball with a different marking, looking surprised on the fairway.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy notices he played the wrong golf ball.

extractedItems.title: Consequences if you hole out with a wrong ball
extractedItems.question: If you putt a wrong ball into the hole on a putting green and don’t fix the mistake, what could happen?

choices.text: Nothing, keep playing
You are given two penalty strokes but keep playing
You could be disqualified
Subtract two strokes from your score

extractedItems.explanation: If you hole a wrong ball and don't rectify the mistake, you could be disqualified.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A distressed teenage girl golfer looking at the hole after realising she finished with the wrong ball on the green.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl looking worried at the golf hole after using wrong ball.

extractedItems.title: Advice about line of play on the green
extractedItems.question: Which of these are NOT allowed when you are putting on the green? (Select all that apply)

choices.text: Your friend tells you how the green breaks
You lay your putter on the green to show your line of play
Your caddie gives you advice about your putt
Your caddie stands directly behind you on your line to help you line up

extractedItems.explanation: You can't get advice about the line of play from fellow players, can't use your putter or other objects to indicate the line, and your caddie can't stand directly behind you on your line to help you line up.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer preparing to putt, while another person tries to give advice, and objects are laid on the green to indicate line. Caddie stands, but not on the direct line.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Teen boy putting on green, someone giving advice, putter showing line, caddie nearby.

Replace the ball to its original spot, no penalty

reviewedItems.title: Penalty for playing the wrong ball
reviewedItems.question: While playing a hole, you hit a shot and then realise you played a ball that isn't yours. What should you do next according to the rules?

choices.text: Keep playing with the wrong ball for the rest of the hole
Stop, find your own ball, play it from where it was, add two penalty strokes, and ignore any strokes made with the wrong ball
Go back to the last tee and replay your shot
Put the wrong ball back where you found it and continue with that ball

reviewedItems.explanation: You must stop and play your own ball from where it lay, adding two penalty strokes. Any strokes made with the wrong ball do not count.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teenage girl golfer on the fairway, looking thoughtfully at a golf ball with a different marking, realising it's not hers.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Teen girl realises she played the wrong golf ball on the fairway.

reviewedItems.title: Consequences if you hole out with a wrong ball
reviewedItems.question: If you putt a wrong ball into the hole on the green and do not fix your mistake before starting the next hole or leaving the green (in stroke play), what can happen?

choices.text: Nothing, you continue the round as normal
You get a two-stroke penalty, but keep playing
You may be disqualified for not correcting the mistake
You subtract two strokes from your score

reviewedItems.explanation: If you do not correct the mistake of holing out with a wrong ball in stroke play, you can be disqualified.

You lay a putter or club on the green to show your intended line
Your caddie stands directly behind you on your line to help you aim
You read your own putt without help
